dedupe_keys.name: retrofit of an air cooled data centre with hot aisle containment turkey 2022

description: This design and retrofit case examines a small open-aisle, air-cooled data centre in Turkey where hot air recirculating over the tops of racks pushed inlet temperatures above the allowable maximum. The team built an open-source computational fluid dynamics model in OpenFOAM, validated it against temperature measurements, used it to diagnose hot-air recirculation and cold-air bypass caused by uneven airflow from the raised-floor plenum, and then retrofitted the room by creating a hot aisle with a moving baffle at the rear of the racks; simulations and new measurements showed better thermal performance, and the study also showed how plenum height and tile perforation rate affect cooling. It was carried out by Design and Simulation Technologies Inc. with Radius Solution Center and published in Case Studies in Thermal Engineering in 2022, with a companion Data in Brief article. Coverage: one small data room before and after the retrofit, including a fictitious 15.5 kW load scenario. Format and access: the article is behind the Elsevier paywall, while the measured temperatures and OpenFOAM cases are free on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: a single small facility; the owner and exact site are not named; energy savings are reported from simulation and short measurements. Simulation uses: hazard exposure of IT equipment to overheating when cooling is degraded or ambient heat rises, design of airflow retrofits, and validated inputs for data-centre thermal digital twins. Related records: AlphaDataCenterCooling and SustainDC model cooling plants, and the OVHcloud Strasbourg fire case shows another facility failure.
